about.purpose: Machine-readable index of this GitHub account. Written for AI assistants (any vendor) and for people arriving cold, so neither has to infer the layout from repo names.
about.subject: Flat-to-VR game modding: converting existing flat PC games to VR, plus the reusable knowledge produced along the way.
about.stated_goal: The playable VR mods matter, but the durable goal is the knowledge, published so others can reuse it.
about.layout_change: 2026-08-30: consolidated from six repos per game (101 repos) to ONE public repo per game plus one private staging monorepo (22 repos). Each former repo is now a folder inside its game repo, with full git history preserved behind a subtree join commit.

headline: 2026-09-14: two cameras found in one day. Dead Space 2's projection is at constant register c4 and Prototype's at c0, both left-handed, both read live through a d3d9 proxy built, self-tested and deployed the same day. Six of the eight projects started on 2026-09-13 were advanced; four of them by static reading alone. The day also produced two corrections to this file's own earlier claims and one account-wide latent bug found in three other projects' proxies.

read_first.if: You are about to drive or automate one of these games
read_first.why: Keys, menu routes, state detection and entry points, per game. Vendor-neutral. Its UNIVERSAL.md carries the method rules that prevent the most wasted work.

read_first.if: You are doing reverse-engineering or VR conversion work
read_first.why: The engine-agnostic PLAYBOOK, the tool catalogue, and tools/ (small utilities that already earned their place).

read_first.if: You want what is known about an engine family
read_first.why: Cross-engine library. docs/engines/ has one page per engine family.

read_first.if: You are resuming work on a specific game
read_first.read: that game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md, then its modding-notes/ folder
read_first.why: The dossier is distilled current truth for that engine, including dead ends. The notes are the chronological ledger.

mod/.holds: release packaging and player-facing docs; the releases themselves are GitHub Releases on the game repo
mod/.note: Often sparse. A project with no release yet has a near-empty mod/; this is expected, not a mistake.

dev-archive/.holds: the live working mod source AND the messy dev history: snapshots, probes, recon evidence, dead ends
dev-archive/.note: This is where the actual mod source lives, commonly under dev-archive/tools/.

modding-notes/.holds: readable field notes and the dated progress ledger

engine-research/.holds: ENGINE-DOSSIER.md — distilled truth about that game's engine, including a dead-ends section

external-research/.holds: leads gathered from public sources by a research-only session; INDEX.md plus topics/

staging.holds: unverified work-in-progress for every project, one folder per game (staging/<prefix>/); the cross-machine handoff channel

conventions.history_note: Each folder was its own repo until 2026-08-30. Full per-file history is preserved and reachable through the folder's subtree join commit (git log the merge parents). The old <prefix>-<suffix> repo names redirect only where a repo was renamed (each game's -mod became the game repo).

session_lanes.note: Five kinds of session, each typed as a slash-command. They are designed to run at the same time; one_writer_per_file below is what keeps them from colliding.

lanes./lm (live modding): the only lane that may launch a game, attach a debugger or drive VR
lanes./pd (parallel development): advances every project as far as it can with no game running
lanes./gr (game research): public-research sweep; curates each game repo external-research/
lanes./gs (github sweep): read-only hygiene audit of the whole estate; curates nothing

background_agents.never_in_includes: the standing /gate-watch background watcher, which is otherwise permitted everywhere (owner ruling, 2026-09-03): those two lanes run fully inline.
background_agents.rationale: The three sweep lanes are breadth-first over many projects and leave their output as reviewable commits. /lm drives a live game, which no agent may do. /gs is an audit whose value is that the session performed each check itself, so a second-hand summary would defeat it.
background_agents.still_applies: Even where allowed, agents must be few and each must have a job the owner could name without asking; ad-hoc fan-out is not the intent.

one_writer_per_file.rule: Every file has exactly one kind of session that may edit it. Reading is unrestricted.

lanes.modding: curates mod/, dev-archive/, modding-notes/, engine-research/ and the staging repo

one_writer_per_file.cross_lane: Contributions travel as new, uniquely-named files dropped in the receiving lane's inbox/ folder — never as edits to a file another lane curates.

HD hands and skin-seam work continues — pass 2 judged “much better” in VR [verified-live 2026-09-06] 2026-09-20 (static): checked against RE4 Remake + Talemann's RE4VR mod. RE2 has NO weapon scope or sight system anywhere in the 494 MB il2cpp dump [measured 2026-09-20], so RE4R's re-pose-the-scope-camera route is closed here too; but via.render.Mirror, updatableMaterial, CapturePlane and RenderOutput are all present, so the Village scope-picture stack would PORT if a sight is ever wanted [inferred-static 2026-09-20]. Working VR sniper scope, accurate and zeroed (flicker gone 2026-09-22). Flat-tested 2026-09-24: the scope starts itself when the rifle is drawn (switched on), the eye pose goes in with the rig so Ethan's clothes no longer show first, and the picture flip needs two presses. Working VR sniper scope; accurate from the hip, and two-handed shots fixed live 2026-09-21 (bullet takes the scope axis from 3 ticks before the shot, dossier 9cd). Found the same day: distance-follow never reached the picture (the exact map is directions-only) -- fixed, and seen reaching the picture in the headset (1.6 deg at 13 m, n=7 shots); eighth zero saved with it on (up -10.7 / right -9.5), near/far then passed the same launch (n=3) and again after a restart with the baked zero loading by itself (n=10 shots, wearer-confirmed); second-day confirmation owed (9ce). Scope picture meant to be 1920x1080 by default for performance, but two runs still rigged 2560 although the word was received -- a missing branch in the size picker, fixed 2026-09-21 and seen taking (1920x1088 latched, not visibly softer). Two-handed grip throw traced to RE8VR applying the whole hand-line rotation in the first gripped frame; grip-no-throw patch worn and working (dossier 9cf); the remaining jump is at the first shot after a take -- the body animation moves the grip socket RE8VR steers by -- socket now frozen at the take, worn and confirmed 2026-09-21 (pre-shot move 4.8 -> ~1.5 deg on 11 of 12 shots; 9cg). Occlusion drift: RE8VR steers from left-hand position only and never reads the OpenXR tracked bit; tracked-bit guard worn 2026-09-21: Virtual Desktop never clears the bit (0 of 365 samples), and the instrument exposed spurious 30-71 deg steering from the day's own relative-grip maths; steering recomputed in the gun's frame, 25 deg limit, FULL/HALF/LOCKED lever (9ci). Wearer reports the large swings predate that bug; RE8VR's steering point is 16 cm out along the left controller and turned by the wrist, so both candidate sources are now logged side by side with a live switch, worn; asked-for steering averaged 27-36 deg, drift work PARKED by Tefa 2026-09-21 (9cj). Remaining: the one-frame flicker and the stepped scope picture -- the flicker measure's Map overran its buffer by 192 bytes and never read anything; repaired, plus a per-second rate watch (picture-changed vs presents, camera-pose-changed vs ticks), worn 2026-09-21: measure works, 18 spikes vs ~20 flickers counted (flicker is in the composed picture; hold 2 block ready, unworn); picture and pose renew every frame, and cropfollow 0 removes the jitter, so the stepping is made by crop placement (9ck). hold 2 worn and does not hide the flicker. One suspect for both: the crop handed game-thread -> present as loose atomics (h_ok false window, torn map, newest-not-matching tick); snapshot hand-off built, not yet worn. Zero moved when the picture size changed 1440p -> 1080p; padded-rows hypothesis disproved (off at 1440p too) (9cl). Snapshot hand-off worn: head-turn stepping GONE, flicker not. Zero traced: applied in the rifle's frame so it turns with cant (as seen -10.9/-9.2 at roll +1, -12.0/-7.7 at roll -4.4), and it numerically equals the eye's off-centre projection (10.0/10.2 deg); view-frame zero installed, not yet worn. START-SCOPE now 720p (9cm). Scope picture equally sharp at 720p/1080p/1440p by eye. Grey-blue wash parked by Tefa until it reappears. Open: a zero that may shift between launches and an intermittent grey-blue wash, both new on 2026-09-21. 2026-09-22 (static + builds): the zero's likely cause -- REFramework plan C draws the mirror from the game's own camera pose while the crop maths used the headset pose off the camera joint; the drawn pose is now exported (REF_GetMirrorDrawPose) and used for the crosshair, default on, self-checking log line (9cn). Stacked grip built: left controller above the right takes the two-handed grip, rifle follows the right hand. Flicker: last good map held over map-less ticks + per-spike map-change instrument. Worn 2026-09-22 11:00: drawn pose only ~2 deg (up) from the joint pose while aiming -- real, not the 10 deg zero; docked shots land with the old zero, stacked shots land low; flicker unchanged. Next zero suspect: the plugin's mirror-plane recompute is 4.0-4.6 deg from the Lua's applied plane (9 deg of aim, rifle-rigid) -- panesrc lever + plane-check line built. Grip: button-only docking, reference at the press, 25 deg limit off (Tefa's asks). Flicker: play-time spikes have a still map, so the frame dump (src/now/prev PPM at the first six spikes) is built. Afternoon DLLs built, not yet installed. Evening: grip settled (button-only dock, snap at the press; universal rule); backwards picture was the drawn-pose switch-off, undone. Flicker ring built + installed: the last 90 shown scope pictures kept on the GPU and dumped to PPM + per-frame numbers when the wearer pulls the trigger (flicker_ring.cpp, FLICKER-CATCH-ON.bat, tools/ring_view.py) -- decides whether the flicker is in the composed picture or after the blit. Evening 3: the upside-down picture since 11:42 was a saved glass_flip_v toggle from four stray panel presses at 11:22 (settings auto-save); every build A/B'd clean first (plan C off, morning plugin, morning-grip framework rebuild); fixed live via the key channel, wearer-confirmed. PD rows: protect orientation knobs from stray presses; deployed Lua drifted from staging. Evening 4: THE FLICKER FOUND -- four hand-caught 90-frame rings, the one odd frame is always the tick whose camera projection read carried the other eye's off-centre term (P[8] sign flipped); eye lock built (majority eye kept, other eye's reads rejected and counted), installed and WORN 18:31: flicker gone (wearer-confirmed), rejections ~10/min in bursts = the old flicker rate (9co). Plan C then switched OFF for good (mirror drawn from the headset): big head-pitch movement gone, small residual parked. Two-shot zero built + installed (shot at a wall, cross on the hole, shot; new zero = old + (bore2 - bore1) as seen; saved as boot value), not worn. PD: skip the prop-arm stage, picture on the rifle the moment it is drawn.

static recon plus a working d3d9 proxy [verified-live 2026-08-25]. The .forge archive format is decoded end to end — container, LZO2A chunks, typed datablocks — by a from-scratch reader in dev-archive/tools/forge [verified-numerically 2026-09-02, 33,401 datafiles]. The camera system is authored as DATA (876 CameraRule entries, one CameraGraph) and a shipped rule CR_Debug_1stPerson is conditioned on a debug first-person state [verified-numerically 2026-09-02]. That rule has now been repointed in a regenerated archive to install a camera that follows the player instead of one that flies itself; deployed, awaiting a walk-and-turn test

FIRST HEADSET RUN 2026-09-10: HEAD TRACKING IS LIVE, position AND rotation, fed from a SteamVR pose per frame [verified-live 2026-09-10, n=1]. The per-eye maths is a transpose of Alan Wake's; the stereo edit, the head offset on all three axes and head rotation (by pre-multiplying rather than rebuilding the view matrix) are all built and verified live. Every stereo hotkey lives on the numpad. What is left is calibration — world scale is still 50 units/metre by feel rather than by measurement

2026-09-14: THE CAMERA IS FOUND [verified-live 2026-09-14, n=1 session]. Register c0, four registers, layout R, LEFT-handed, aspect exactly 16/9, X not mirrored, near plane 0.300000, far plane 7500, 80.00 degrees horizontal, with a zoom ladder of eight fields of view all at exactly 16:9. The depth term FITS the textbook left-handed form, unlike Dead Space 2's, so per-eye maths can use the standard formulae. The game also ships READABLE HLSL SOURCE in shaders.rcf naming its own constants (p3dWorldViewProjectionMatrix). CORRECTION: that source implied a fused world-view-projection, but the gameplay matrix at c0 is a PURE projection - registers are assigned per shader and the shipped file is a 10 KB sample. Open: where the view transform lives (the c0+5 upload, the most frequent of all, is unread).

2026-09-14: CDebugConsole is a real class, not a stray string, and beside it sit CGameDebugMenu and CFreeCamera [inferred-static 2026-09-14]. The camera is a named registered object (CCamera, CCameraComponent, CCameraPlanesParameters, CStaticCamera, plus cutscene, quest and animation camera families). Config ships as plain text in bin/config - about 30 named [Rendering] switches, Fullscreen among them, so windowed mode needs no code patch; [Engine] CustomRenderingSettings ships at 0 and is worth flipping. No stereo/VR key appears in the shipped section. Module base is FIXED (ASLR off) and d3d9 is a STATIC import, so a proxy DLL is an available route. WARNING: d3dx9_39 does NOT include D3DXGetShaderConstantTable, so no free route to named shader constants here. How any of the three debug facilities opens is unknown - debug classes routinely survive into retail builds with their entry points removed.

projects.developer: Bloober Team (published by Konami); remake of Team Silent’s 2001 original
projects.stage: First live session 2026-09-19: the game runs, is forced to a measured 1280x720 window, and UEVR injects and opens a stereo OpenXR session (1668x1856 per eye) [verified-live 2026-09-19, n=1]. Engine confirmed as UE 5.1.1 twice independently. Anti-tamper audited statically and the executable is clean [measured 2026-09-19] - no packer, empty TLS callbacks, CFG not enforced - though the game reportedly shipped with Denuvo, so a future patch is the risk rather than the present state. The existing community profile was mapped in full: 49,718 lines of Lua, mostly a shared cross-game framework, driving Unreal's own two-bone IK solver across the script boundary per arm per frame on a poseable puppet of the whole clothed body - its own comments record the precision loss and the performance workarounds. Our mod is therefore being built as a native C++ UEVR plugin with Lua only filling gaps, which is also what makes using the game's own interaction hand animations feasible. PureDark's AFW build is an optional comfort add-on, never a dependency. Nothing seen in a headset yet; the dev PC has none.

projects.injection: our own static recompilation of the Xbox 360 release - there has never been a PC version
projects.stage: Our own build plays real-time 3D [verified-live 2026-09-16] and produces a measured left/right stereo pair [verified-live 2026-09-18]. DECIDED 2026-09-18: geometry stereo, one eye per guest frame with the world held still for the second eye; depth reprojection is the named fallback. The eye offset lives in the camera (which is also where head tracking will go), and the world-freeze is built - the guest clock pin is verified engaging, though its on-screen effect is not yet confirmed. One world unit is about an inch, so half an IPD is 1.25 units. default.xex unpacks in 80 lines of Python, giving 45,101 readable strings and a 21,414-function index; the engine is Starbreeze XReality. Next: prove the freeze visually, side-by-side composition at the presenter, then OpenXR. Nothing seen in a headset yet. Tefa's stated top VR want. The game and our port are now set up on the faster test machine, so the real frame rate can be measured there [verified-live 2026-09-20]. Home-PC frame rate measured 2026-09-21: ~180-285 fps in the opening car scene (two measures disagree; both far above what stereo needs).

notes_for_ai_readers: Folder presence varies: a missing folder means that stage has not been reached yet.
Prefer ai-game-control-profiles over inferring controls from these repos — the game repos describe how a game was MODIFIED, not how to OPERATE it.
Every game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md has a dead-ends section. Read it before proposing an approach; several plausible-looking routes have already been tried and refuted.
Claims in the notes carry dates. Where a later entry contradicts an earlier one, the later entry wins and usually says so explicitly.
